title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: What is the core difference between a workflow and an agent?

options.text: A workflow only answers questions, but an agent is any system that uses tools
A workflow calls the model once, but an agent calls the model many times
A workflow's steps are set in code, but an agent's model picks its next step
A workflow runs on a smaller model, but an agent needs a larger model

items.stem: Your code always runs three steps in order: search the manual, one model call to draft an answer, a second model call to check the draft. What is this system?

options.text: A workflow, since the code fixes the order of the steps
An agent, since it makes more than one model call
An agent, since it searches the manual with a tool
An agent, since the model reviews its own draft

items.stem: After each result, the makerspace assistant's model chooses whether to check the calendar, ask the student a question, book, or stop. Who owns the control flow (who decides the next step): the code or the model?
Which makerspace task is the best fit for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Answering any question a student asks about any machine in the shop
Before each booking, look it up, fill a template, and send a reminder
Working out why a student's print failed when the cause is not known
Planning a project that may need several machines in an order not known

items.stem: A fixed workflow makes exactly 3 model calls per request. An agent on the same task averages 8 calls; every call costs $0.002. How many dollars more does the agent cost over 500 requests?
Every booking runs the same three steps: check the calendar, confirm with the student, write the booking. A teammate wants an agent "for flexibility"; what is your best reply?

options.text: Agree, since an agent is safer because the model can double-check each step
Agree, since any system that calls tools counts as an agent anyway
Disagree, since a workflow is always the better choice over an agent
Disagree, since known steps can be fixed in code at lower cost and risk
